title: Run a catering business that is safe and profitable

say: Run a catering business that is safe and profitable.
This is the video for Module 5 of Advanced Cooking and Nutrition: running a home catering and food products business.
Many caterers lose clients not because the food was poor, but because the queue was long, or food ran out on one side of the hall.

say: Keep gas cylinders upright, outdoors or well ventilated, away from the flame and from guests. Check hoses and connections with soapy water. Bubbles mean a leak. Never use a lighter to check.
Keep a fire extinguisher and fire blanket at the cooking area.

Turn off the valve, put out all flames, do not switch electrics on or off, move people away.

say: When you buy yam, plantain or fish, peel, bones and trimmings are lost. First, weigh what you buy. That is the as purchased weight.

panel.heading: Yield: you do not serve all you buy
items: Weigh what you buy (as purchased)
Trim, cook and weigh what you serve
Yield % = served ÷ bought × 100
Record your own yields; retest often

say: Then trim, cook and weigh what you can actually serve. That is the edible portion.

say: Contribution margin is selling price minus food cost. Sort every dish by how many sold and by its margin.
A star is popular with a high margin, so keep it exactly the same. A plowhorse is popular with a low margin. Raise the price slightly or cut a costly component.

A puzzle has a high margin but few sales, so photograph it better and recommend it. A dog is unpopular and low margin. Remove or redesign it. Repeat this every month or two, because prices change quickly.
Register your business with CAC and file annual returns. Packaged products like spice blends need NAFDAC registration, so get requirements from NAFDAC directly, not social media agents.
Ask your local government about health permits. Keep supplier, temperature, cleaning and complaints records, written at the time.
Use a written agreement for every event, and never claim a food cures anything.

panel.heading: What clients and inspectors expect
items: CAC registration and annual returns
NAFDAC registration for packaged products
Local health permits as required
Supplier, temperature and cleaning records
Written client agreements; no health claims

say: To remember. Plan staff and lines from guest numbers. Treat gas with respect. Keep hot food above 60 C.
Price each plate from its true food cost. And keep records and written agreements, because they protect you and your clients.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Plan servers and buffet lines by guest numbers
Smell gas? Valve off, flames out, people away
Hot food above 60 C; 2 hours out means discard
Price = food cost per plate ÷ target %
Records and agreements protect you
